memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Understand, then, that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people. Remember this and never forget how you aroused the anger of the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day you left Egypt until you arrived here, you have been rebellious against the Lord. - Deut 9:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses drives the point home with striking honesty. Not only is Israel receiving the land apart from their righteousness — they are actually a "stiff-necked people," rebellious from the day they left Egypt right up to the present. The image of a "stiff neck" comes from a stubborn animal that refuses to be led, resisting the gentle guidance of its master. This was God's blunt assessment of His people: chronically stubborn, repeatedly rebellious. And yet He was still bringing them into the land.

There is something deeply freeing about this honesty. God does not pretend His people are better than they are. He sees them clearly — their stubbornness, their rebellion, their long track record of failure — and He chooses to bless them anyway, by grace. This means God's kindness toward us is not based on Him overlooking our flaws or being unaware of our sin. He knows the worst about us, and still He loves and keeps us.

We sometimes fear that if God really knew how stubborn and sinful we are, He would give up on us. But He already knows. He sees every rebellious streak, every stiff-necked moment, and He has made a way for us anyway through Christ. Jesus did not die for people who had their act together, but for the ungodly (Rom 5:6). This does not excuse our stubbornness — Moses calls Israel to remember and repent — but it assures us that God's grace runs deeper than our worst. You are not too stubborn for God's patient, persevering love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I honest with myself and God about my own stubbornness and sin?
- How does it comfort me that God blesses His people knowing the worst about them?
- Where do I need to stop resisting God's gentle leading in my life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see my stubbornness clearly, and yet You love me still. Thank You that Your grace runs deeper than my worst rebellion. Soften my stiff neck, help me stop resisting Your leading, and draw me close by Your patient love. Amen.
